source_name: Komerční banka – Pro investory (IR hub, CZ)
why_relevant: Root of the single most structured issuer IR estate in Czech banking. Fans out to Výkazy a výsledky, Hospodářské výsledky, Finanční kalendář, Akcionáři/akcie/dividendy, Ratings, and Povinně uveřejňované informace. KB is the only one of the four systemic banks with its own PSE-listed equity, so its IR discipline is the highest and it is the natural anchor node for the whole cell.

source_name: Komerční banka – Hospodářské výsledky (quarterly results archive 2000–present)
why_relevant: The densest single page in the cell. Year-collapsible archive back to 2000 carrying, per quarter: results presentation PDF, Czech commentary on business results, consolidated IFRS financial statements (PDF and XLSX), individual statements with audit report, and a 'facts and figures' spreadsheet. The XLSX layer is the reason this outranks everything else — machine-readable time series of a systemic Czech bank without any parsing of prose.

source_name: Komerční banka – Výroční a pololetní zprávy (annual & half-year reports, 1998–present, ESEF/XBRL)
why_relevant: Audited annual financial reports and half-year reports going back to 1998, grouped by five-year blocks. From 2020 onward each annual report is offered in ESEF, XBRL/HTML and PDF — the only confirmed machine-readable structured filing format in this cell. Since 2024 the CSRD non-financial statement is folded into the annual financial report, so sustainability disclosure is collected here too rather than separately.

source_name: Komerční banka – Finanční kalendář (financial calendar)
why_relevant: Publishes upcoming and past investor events — results release dates, conference calls, general meeting. This is the scheduling backbone for the whole cell: it tells a collector when to go looking rather than polling blindly, and it is the only confirmed dedicated calendar page among the four banks (ČS embeds its calendar inside a results page; ČSOB and UniCredit CZ appear to have none).

source_name: Komerční banka – Povinně uveřejňované informace (mandatory disclosures)
why_relevant: The regulatory-announcement layer distinct from the marketing IR layer. Confirmed children: Akcionáři KB (holders above 1% of share capital), Politika odměňování (board remuneration), Informační povinnost obchodníka s cennými papíry, Informace o cenných papírech (KB's own and clients' bond issues), Informace o bance, and NRB COVID III support recipients. Ownership, remuneration and issuance data live here and nowhere else on the site.

source_name: Komerční banka – Akcionáři, akcie a dividendy / Valné hromady
why_relevant: Carries KB share data, shareholder structure and bylaws, and the general-meeting record including dividend resolutions, record dates and payment dates. General-meeting materials are the earliest formal signal of capital-return policy and board composition changes — e.g. the 2026 AGM approved a gross dividend of CZK 95.60/share and enlarged the supervisory board from 9 to 12 members.

source_name: Komerční banka – IR novinky (investor news / regulatory announcement feed)
why_relevant: Per-item permalinks for each regulatory announcement, including the quarterly 'Hospodářské výsledky ke dni DD.MM.YYYY' releases and funding events such as covered-bond issuance. This is the fastest-updating KB surface and the best change-detection target; the results page and the annual-report page lag it.

source_name: Komerční banka – Tiskové zprávy / Pro média (press centre)
why_relevant: Corporate press releases including AGM outcomes, product and channel launches, partnerships and cyber/fraud campaigns. Complements the IR feed: commercial and strategic moves that never reach a results deck surface here first. English mirror exists at /en/about-bank/press-releases.

source_name: Komerční banka – Ratings & Facts and Results (fact book equivalent)
why_relevant: KB is the only bank in this cell with a discoverable dedicated ratings page (financial and non-financial/ESG ratings) plus a 'Facts and Results' / KB group key financial information page that functions as a lightweight fact book. Ratings changes are a leading indicator on funding cost; the key-financials page gives a pre-aggregated KPI set that avoids re-deriving ratios from statements.

source_name: Komerční banka – Udržitelnost / Report o udržitelnosti (CSRD sustainability reporting)
why_relevant: KB issued its 2024 sustainability report on a CSRD/ESRS basis and runs a dedicated ESG regulation section. Relevant to disclosure tracking because from 2024 the non-financial statement migrated into the annual financial report while the standalone sustainability reports remain the archive for earlier years — a reporting-boundary change a collector must model explicitly or it will silently lose the ESG series.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Hospodářské výsledky (results hub + financial calendar)
why_relevant: ČS's primary results surface. Carries 'Termíny zveřejnění hospodářských výsledků' (the publication-date calendar, flagged as provisional) and 'Klíčové údaje o České spořitelně', and routes by year into the document repository. ČS is the largest Czech bank by clients, so this is a must-own node even though the page is a router rather than a document store.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Dokumenty ke stažení (document repository, deep-link anchors)
why_relevant: The actual document store behind ČS's whole disclosure estate — annual reports, results presentations, price lists, mandatory disclosures, and a Debt Investors & MREL category. Categories are addressed by stable numeric IDs in the URL fragment (e.g. #/18/Prezentace-hospodarskych-vysledku for results presentations, #/1124/Debt-Investors-and-MREL, #/1509/2026 for the 2026 results set), which makes it deep-linkable once the app renders.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – For shareholders and investors (IR page, EN)
why_relevant: The closest thing ČS has to a conventional IR landing page and the only place a named IR contact was found for the bank (Juraj Garaj, IR Manager). Links out to shareholder structure, current rating, the financial calendar, a general corporate presentation PDF, and the Debt Investors & MREL document set — the last being the most analytically useful, since ČS's own equity is not listed and debt disclosure is where bank-level detail concentrates.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Výroční zprávy (annual report PDFs, static path)
why_relevant: ČS annual reports are served as static PDFs on predictable /static_internet/ paths with a vz-YYYY.pdf filename convention, which sidesteps the JavaScript document app entirely for the single most important document per year. Note the directory segment has changed over time (older years sit under .../Obecne_informace/FSCS/...), so path templating must be per-era, not global.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Tiskové zprávy / Pro média
why_relevant: ČS's earnings narrative reaches the public through press releases before the document repository is refreshed, and the URL carries the publication date in the path (/YYYY/MM/DD/slug), which makes date-bounded crawling and backfill straightforward. Also republishes Erste Group-level results in the ČS context, linking the local and group narratives.

source_name: ČSOB – Vztahy k investorům (investor relations)
why_relevant: ČSOB's declared investor-relations entry point. ČSOB Group is one of the three largest Czech banking groups by loan and deposit volume, so its disclosure record is non-optional for this cell. Could not be rendered on this pass — the page is a hypothesis pending the deterministic verification run, not a confirmed dead end.

source_name: ČSOB – Povinně uveřejňované informace (mandatory disclosures & annual report archive)
why_relevant: The statutory disclosure page carrying ČSOB's annual reports; search evidence shows an archive spanning at least 2013 to 2025, with the 2025 report published 23 April 2026 and 2024 on 23 April 2025 — a stable late-April cadence a collector can schedule against. Because ČSOB has no listed equity of its own, this mandatory-disclosure page rather than an equity IR site is the authoritative local record.

source_name: ČSOB – Tiskové zprávy / Servis pro média (results press releases, tzYYMMDD.pdf)
why_relevant: This is where ČSOB Group's quarterly and full-year results actually land locally — as dated press-release PDFs on a highly regular filename convention, tzYYMMDD.pdf under /documents/10710/{folderId}/. Given ČSOB publishes no local results deck, these PDFs plus the KBC group quarterly report are the complete ČSOB earnings record. The filename convention makes the asset layer predictable even while the listing page resists fetching.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia – Výroční zprávy / Annual reports
why_relevant: The statutory reporting home for the fourth systemic bank. Carries both annual reports and half-year financial reports in parallel Czech and English editions on a stable CDN path. The half-year reports are explicitly published under §119 of Czech Act No. 256/2004 Coll. and §35 of Slovak Act No. 429/2002 Z.z. — a useful reminder that this issuer is dual-jurisdiction and its disclosures cover a merged CZ+SK balance sheet, so CZ-only figures must be segmented, not read off the cover.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia – Debt Investor Relations (prospectuses)
why_relevant: UniCredit Bank CZ&SK has no listed equity and therefore no earnings-call apparatus; its only investor-facing channel beyond statutory reports is debt investor relations — base prospectuses, issuance programmes and supplements. For funding-strategy and covered-bond intelligence on this issuer, this page is the sole primary source in the cell.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG – Investor Relations / Financial Reports (ČS segment)
why_relevant: Česká spořitelna publishes no quarterly results deck or earnings call of its own; the analytical layer for ČS lives at its parent. Erste's IR estate supplies, per quarter, an IR News release, an interim report, an XLSX key-financials data sheet, separate teleconference and press-conference presentations, and audio and video webcasts — with a Czech Republic segment broken out. The XLSX and the segment tables are the highest-value machine-readable ČS series available anywhere.

source_name: KBC Group NV – Investor Relations / Quarterly Reports (Czech Republic segment, ČSOB)
why_relevant: The presentation and segment-analysis layer ČSOB itself does not publish. KBC's quarterly report and company presentation break out a Czech Republic segment net result each quarter (e.g. EUR 244m in 3Q2025, EUR 207m in 1Q2025, EUR 238m in 4Q2024), plus goodwill and FX effects attributed to ČSOB. Also useful for the Slovak side following the ČSOB / 365.bank combination. Effectively mandatory as the ČSOB counterpart to Erste-for-ČS.

source_name: Kurzy.cz / Patria.cz – issuer regulatory-announcement mirrors for Czech banks
why_relevant: Both portals republish Czech issuers' mandatory announcements verbatim, including 'Výroční zpráva za rok YYYY' notices for Komerční banka and Česká spořitelna and ČSOB Group results summaries. Two uses: as a change-detection tripwire that fires when an issuer publishes, and as a fallback read path when the issuer's own site is bot-defended — which, in this cell, csob.cz and unicreditbank.cz both are. Treat as a pointer to the primary document, never as the document of record.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Investor Relations portal (investors.moneta.cz)
why_relevant: MONETA is the only domestically listed (Prague Stock Exchange) issuer in this cell and therefore runs a full IR machine: quarterly results, presentations, transcripts, dividend policy, AGM documents, ratings, bond documentation and an analyst list. It is the single richest, most structured, highest-cadence disclosure source for a second-tier Czech bank and sets the benchmark against which the non-listed peers' thinner disclosure can be measured. The portal is bilingual (cs/en) with parallel document sets.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Financial results & mandatory disclosures (quarterly packs, Pillar 3)
source_subtype: issuer periodic financial reporting / Pillar 3 disclosure page
why_relevant: The operational core of MONETA's disclosure: per-quarter presentation PDFs, interim/half-year financial reports, 'basic data' spreadsheets, press releases and conference-call transcripts back to roughly 2011, plus the mandatory-disclosure block (ČNB Decree 163/2014, CRR 575/2013 capital adequacy, MREL) reachable via the #mandatory-disclosures anchor. Subsidiary reporting (MONETA Stavební Spořitelna, MONETA Auto, MONETA Leasing, Wüstenrot hypoteční banka) is published alongside, which gives visibility into mortgage/leasing/building-society channels. The Excel 'basic data' files make this one of the few machine-parsable series in the cell. Note moneta.cz/o-nas/informacni-povinnost 301-redirects here.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Servis pro média / Tiskové zprávy (press releases, archived by year)
why_relevant: Where MONETA announces product, branch, ATM, digital-channel and payments moves that never reach the IR pack, plus the plain-language versions of results announcements. Year-partitioned archives (observed dedicated pages for 2021, 2022 and an 'older' archive) give a multi-year press-release corpus in one place — the best narrative-change detector for this issuer.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (CZ) – Výsledky hospodaření hub (annual / half-year / quarterly)
why_relevant: This is the URL ČNB itself names as Raiffeisenbank's mandatory-disclosure location. It fans out into annual reports, half-year financial reports and quarterly filings, and — unusually valuable — it also preserves the results of absorbed banks (Equa bank through 2021, eBanka pre-merger), which makes it an M&A-continuity source for reconstructing the Czech second tier's consolidation history. Raiffeisenbank is now the largest bank in this cell by balance sheet after the Equa bank integration.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (CZ) – Informace pro investory / RBCZ investor presentations
why_relevant: Raiffeisenbank CZ is not listed but issues debt and produces a standalone country-level investor presentation deck (observed path /attachments/pi/rbi/rbcz-investor-presentation-<YYYY>q<N>.pdf). These decks are far more analytical than the statutory annual report — segment splits, loan-book composition, digital/channel KPIs — and are the closest thing to IR-grade material outside MONETA in this cell. English-language, quarterly cadence.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (CZ) – Tiskové zprávy / Informační servis pro média
why_relevant: Deeply year- and quarter-partitioned press archive (observed paths of the form /tiskove-zpravy/tiskove-zpravy-<YEAR>/tiskove-zpravy-<YEAR><QUARTER>/<DDMMYYYY>-<slug>), which is unusually crawler-friendly and date-stamped in the URL itself. Carries both the results announcements (e.g. FY profit releases) and the product/payments/third-party-partner announcements that reveal channel strategy. Also a media asset download page.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG – group quarterly & annual reports (CZ segment)
source_subtype: foreign parent group investor relations (segment reporting)
why_relevant: RBI reports the Czech Republic as a named CEE segment with its own P&L, loan/deposit volumes and risk metrics, at listed-issuer cadence and quality, and management commentary on the Czech outlook surfaces on the group earnings calls. This gives a second, independently audited read on Raiffeisenbank CZ that arrives faster than the local statutory annual report and is directly comparable across CEE peers.

source_name: Air Bank a.s. – Konsolidované výroční zprávy (direct PDF series)
why_relevant: Air Bank is the PPF group's Czech retail challenger and one of the most-copied UX/pricing innovators in the market, but it is unlisted and discloses thinly. Its consolidated annual reports (IFRS, audited, prepared under §22b and §19a(7)/§23a(2) of Act 563/1991 Sb.) are nonetheless published as clean standalone PDFs going back to at least 2011 on a stable /file-download/ path — the deepest continuous statutory series available for this bank. Caveat found while fetching: the ČNB-designated mandatory-disclosure page (/dokumenty-ke-stazeni) surfaces price lists, rate overviews, T&Cs and complaint rules but does NOT visibly link the annual reports; the report PDFs are reachable directly.

source_name: Air Bank a.s. – Novinky / Pro novináře (press room)
why_relevant: Air Bank does not publish quarterly results locally, so its press room is the primary high-frequency signal for the bank: mobile-app redesigns, client-count milestones, campaign/positioning shifts and product launches. Observed releases quantify digital-channel usage (weekly active mobile-app users), which is exactly the kind of channel metric systemic banks bury.

source_name: PPF Group – press releases & annual accounts (Air Bank Group financial results)
source_subtype: parent holding company disclosure / press release archive
why_relevant: PPF publishes 'Air Bank Group' combined financial results as standalone releases (net profit, net loan portfolio, YoY growth) ahead of and independently of the statutory annual report, and its group annual accounts describe the Czech banking contribution (PPF banka and Air Bank) alongside Home Credit CZ/SK. For an unlisted bank this is the only quasi-IR narrative available, and it is the natural place to detect ownership/perimeter changes.

source_name: Fio banka a.s. – Povinně uveřejňované informace (quarterly XLSX + annual reports)
source_subtype: bank statutory disclosure page with structured data files
why_relevant: The best machine-readable disclosure in the entire cell. Fio publishes the ČNB-mandated quarterly disclosure annexes as raw .xlsx files on a highly predictable path (FB<YEAR>_q<N>_priloha_<K>.xlsx), plus annual reports every year back to 2006 published by 30 April, plus non-financial information under §32g of the Accounting Act, audit-committee details, cash-flow statements and capital-adequacy reports. Fio is also a payments-relevant actor (large free-transfer retail base and a brokerage arm), so its quarterly annexes are a clean quantitative series for a challenger bank.

source_name: Fio banka a.s. – Tiskové zprávy / Aktuality (media service)
why_relevant: Fio narrates its own results in press releases (client counts, net profit, balance-sheet total, digitalisation and anti-cybercrime priorities) that predate and summarise the formal annual report. Detail URLs carry a numeric article id, so the archive is enumerable. Two URL families were observed for the same content (/o-nas/media/... and /spolecnost-fio/media/...), which a collector must reconcile.

source_name: Fio banka – Zpravodajství / Zprávy z burzy (sell-side coverage of MONETA)
why_relevant: Fio's brokerage desk publishes 'Projekce hospodaření' pre-earnings previews for MONETA Money Bank every quarter — analyst consensus expectations for net interest income, fees and profit, plus the exact release time and management conference-call time. This is one of very few Czech-language sell-side series on a domestic bank, and it gives both a benchmark to compare actuals against and a reliable early warning of MONETA's reporting calendar. Dual-role source: Fio is simultaneously an actor in this cell and a publisher about it.

source_name: Banka CREDITAS a.s. – Povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: CREDITAS is now the most dynamic consolidator in the Czech second tier — it absorbed Max banka and acquired the Maltese MeDirect group, and reported a step-change in profit for 2025. It is a bond issuer, so it publishes a full 'Výroční finanční zpráva' and a 'Pololetní finanční zpráva' rather than only a plain annual report. ČNB designates this page as its mandatory-disclosure location. Direct fetch returned HTTP 403 — the site appears bot-defended rather than absent, since individual document PDFs on the same host resolve in search results.

source_name: Trinity Bank a.s. – Povinně zveřejňované informace (2012–2025, bilingual)
source_subtype: bank statutory disclosure page with structured data files
why_relevant: A small, purely Czech-owned niche bank with a surprisingly complete and long disclosure archive: annual reports 2012–2025 (English editions from 2020 onward), quarterly 'Informace o Trinity Bank k <date>' files in .xlsx, half-year reports for some years, and multi-part capital-adequacy annexes. The Excel quarterly series makes it directly comparable to Fio's annexes, giving two structured small-bank benchmarks. Note the URL contains 'zverejovane' (one 'ň' dropped) — an easy typo trap for a collector.

source_name: Partners Banka a.s. – Dokumenty ke stažení (disclosure + shareholder materials)
why_relevant: The newest bank in the cell (market launch March 2024) and an aggressive payments/product first mover — multi-currency account across ~15 currencies, in-app bitcoin purchase, frequent savings-rate repricing. Its download hub carries quarterly mandatory disclosures, annual reports 2022–2025 in Czech and English, capital-adequacy information in the Czech Banking Association standard format, shareholder-meeting invitations and annual-report summaries, plus rate sheets and pre-contractual disclosures. An explicitly maintained archive of superseded documents makes historical T&C and pricing diffing possible.

source_name: Partners Banka a.s. – Pro média (press room)
why_relevant: Partners Banka announces feature launches and milestone metrics here at high frequency, and the releases carry hard numbers (client counts, salary-crediting clients, deposit volumes, anniversary stats). Because the bank is new, this press room is effectively its growth-trajectory dataset. Product announcements observed include a multi-currency account and term deposits with named headline rates — direct payments-and-pricing intelligence.

source_name: Partners Financial Services a.s. – parent group documents & EU growth prospectus
why_relevant: Partners Banka's owner publishes its own annual reports (2022–2024 observed) and, critically, an EU Growth Prospectus for its shares that contains the banking-project rationale, capitalisation plan and risk factors — the kind of forward-looking strategic document a bank's own statutory annual report never contains. The group has stated an intention to list on the Prague Stock Exchange, so this source may upgrade to a full IR channel; worth monitoring for that transition.

source_name: Max banka a.s. – legacy mandatory-disclosure archive (now a CREDITAS product line)
why_relevant: Max banka no longer exists as an independent bank — it merged into Banka CREDITAS and maxbanka.eu now presents itself as the 'Max' product line of Banka CREDITAS. The page nonetheless still serves a complete historical archive: annual reports 2010–2023, ČBA-format quarterly filings 2021–2024 (latest observed 30 Sep 2024), and disclosure annexes back to 2015. This is a closing time-window: valuable to harvest now for the pre-merger baseline of a bank that also carries the earlier Expobank CZ lineage, and likely to be retired. Its news section also documented the merger mechanics (bank code 4000 to 2250, instant payments introduction).

source_name: mBank CZ – tiskové centrum (dedicated Czech press portal on the group media domain)
why_relevant: mBank operates in the Czech Republic as a branch of the Polish mBank S.A. under the EU single-licence regime, so it files no Czech statutory annual report of its own — which makes this Czech-language press portal (hosted on the Polish group's media domain, an easy source to miss) the main direct channel for CZ-specific announcements on products, pricing, mortgages and digital channels. Complemented by the consumer-facing blog/aktuality section on mbank.cz and the product document library.

source_name: mBank S.A. Group – Investor Relations (Czech & Slovak foreign-branch segment reporting)
source_subtype: foreign parent group investor relations (segment reporting)
why_relevant: Because mBank CZ is a branch, its financials exist only inside mBank S.A. Group reporting — and the group does break out 'foreign branches in the Czech Republic and Slovakia' with gross profit, client counts and product-sales commentary inside the Retail Banking segment of its Management Board Report and consolidated quarterly reports. This is the only credible quantitative window on mBank's Czech business, and it is listed-issuer grade. Caveat: CZ and SK are reported together, so Czech-only figures usually must be inferred.

source_name: ČNB – Přehled odkazů na webové stránky bank obsahující povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: The single highest-leverage pointer for this entire workstream: the regulator itself maintains the authoritative, curated list of every licensed Czech bank's mandatory-disclosure URL. One fetch resolved the correct disclosure page for Raiffeisenbank, MONETA, Air Bank, Fio, Banka CREDITAS, Trinity Bank, Max banka and Partners Banka simultaneously — eliminating guesswork about which of a bank's many pages is the statutory one. It doubles as a change-detector: entries appearing or disappearing signal licence grants, mergers and wind-downs. Roughly two dozen banks are listed, so it also defines the universe boundary for the domestic-licence cohort.

source_name: ČNB – Centrální úložiště regulovaných informací (central repository of regulated information)
source_subtype: officially appointed mechanism (OAM) for regulated information
why_relevant: The statutory single point of access for regulated information filed by issuers of listed securities under Act 256/2004 Sb. and MAR (Regulation 596/2014). It is the regulator-side capture of exactly what MONETA (listed equity) and Banka CREDITAS / Raiffeisenbank (bond issuers) must file — annual financial reports, half-year reports, inside information. Because filing here is a legal obligation, it is more complete and better time-stamped than any corporate website, and it catches issuers in this cell that have no IR page at all. A direct fetch failed with a socket hang up, which for cnb.cz is far more likely transient/bot-related than an indication the page is gone.

source_name: ČNB – JERRS, Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (+ WS JERRS API, open data)
source_subtype: regulator entity registry with API and open data
why_relevant: The authoritative entity registry: every licensed bank, foreign-bank branch and payment institution, searchable by name, IČO and registered office, with an as-of date so historical states can be reconstructed. Crucially it exposes machine interfaces — WS JERRS web services (available since 1 July 2019) and a ČNB open-data section — which turns actor-map maintenance into an automated job rather than manual curation. Essential for keeping this cell's roster correct as banks merge (Max banka), wind down (Hello bank) or enter (Partners Banka).

source_name: or.justice.cz – Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (commercial register collection of deeds)
source_subtype: national company register / statutory document repository
why_relevant: The legal backstop for every unlisted bank in this cell. Czech law requires accounting entities in the public register to deposit annual financial statements and annual reports in the Sbírka listin, free to access without registration, as downloadable PDFs. This catches filings that a bank has quietly dropped from its own website, provides the audited statutory version rather than the marketing 'graphic' edition, and supplies board/ownership changes and merger deeds — exactly what is needed to date events like the Max banka absorption into Banka CREDITAS. Also the only route to documents for entities that publish nothing voluntarily.
